rights.completion_rule: All checklist items true, reviewer identity/qualification/date populated, and decision pass or pass-with-limitations.
limitations: Use only citation metadata, canonical URLs/DOIs, bibliographic facts, and project-authored summaries.
Do not ingest, chunk, redistribute, or store copyrighted source excerpts unless a separate documented rights basis exists.
Metadata-only evidence must not be described as excerpt validation, source-text hash validation, or copyright/license clearance.
Open-access or Creative Commons indicators must be verified per source before any broader reuse.
Rights approval does not by itself approve production release, assessment eligibility, or final question promotion.

technical.qualification_reference: Former post-secondary automotive instructor with over six years of automotive instruction; automotive/diesel technician background; retired Army heavy equipment repair leader/technician.
technical.completion_rule: All checklist items true, reviewer identity/qualification/date populated, and decision pass or pass-with-limitations.
limitations: The 20 questions remain conceptual/formative training questions and do not authorize vehicle service procedures.
Vehicle-specific thresholds, electrical-state verification, isolation steps, PPE, test points, acceptance criteria, and procedures must come from applicable authoritative information.
No single DTC, measurement, symptom, state estimate, communication fault, charging condition, or other observation establishes component failure by itself.
Request -> Measure -> Compare -> Correlate -> Verify remains an AutoLearnPro project-authored diagnostic framework.
Technical approval does not approve citations, rights, safety, instructional quality, production use, or assessment eligibility.

instructional.qualification_reference: Former post-secondary automotive instructor with over six years of experience teaching automotive systems, diagnostics, electrical/electronics, engine performance, climate control, brakes, drivetrain, suspension/steering, and transmission courses.
instructional.completion_rule: All checklist items true, reviewer identity/qualification/date populated, and decision pass or pass-with-limitations.
limitations: The 20 items remain formative training content and are not institutional or high-stakes assessment items.
Difficulty labels may be recalibrated later using learner-performance data, but analytics must not substitute for technical, safety, or rights review.
Learner feedback should continue emphasizing evidence correlation, uncertainty, and applicable vehicle-specific information.
Distractors must continue avoiding unsafe service shortcuts, universal procedures, or component replacement from a single clue.
Instructional approval does not approve rights, safety, citation validation, production release, or assessment eligibility.

safety.qualification_reference: Former post-secondary automotive instructor and automotive/diesel technician with experience teaching shop safety, electrical/electronics, diagnostics, and hands-on automotive laboratory procedures.
safety.completion_rule: All checklist items true, reviewer identity/qualification/date populated, and decision pass or pass-with-limitations.
limitations: AUT-250 remains conceptual/formative training and does not replace manufacturer or workplace safety procedures.
High-voltage isolation, discharge or wait times, PPE selection, meter category or rating, test points, and acceptance criteria remain vehicle- or component-specific.
No learner response or feedback authorizes component removal, high-voltage access, energized testing, or bypass of protection systems.
Diagnostic evidence may justify further investigation but does not authorize unsafe physical action.
Safety approval does not approve rights, citation validation, production release, or assessment eligibility.

questions.claim_review: A battery data set shows one cell-group voltage differing from neighboring groups during the same operating state. What is the most defensible next interpretation?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Cell-group differences are treated as evidence to correlate with state, trends, and related battery data; no single observation is treated as failure proof.

questions.claim_review: A battery state-of-health estimate changes noticeably from an earlier record. What should be compared before using that change to support a repair decision?
questions.source_applicability_notes: SOH remains an estimated/calculated state; interpretation is tied to inputs, context, and trend rather than a universal replacement rule.

questions.claim_review: A battery-management system reports a cell-imbalance condition. Which evidence best helps evaluate whether a meaningful difference is actually present?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Cell-group voltage evidence is appropriate for evaluating an imbalance hypothesis when compared under relevant operating context.

questions.claim_review: Before deciding that a battery temperature reading is abnormal, what information should be requested or established first?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Battery temperature is interpreted with operating context and applicable vehicle criteria; wording avoids universal limits.

questions.claim_review: Which evidence set best supports investigation of a possible power-electronics thermal concern?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Power-electronics temperature is correlated with operating state and thermal behavior rather than treated as an isolated pass/fail value.

questions.claim_review: A DC-DC converter measured response differs from the commanded or expected response. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Command-response disagreement is diagnostic evidence requiring validation and correlation; it does not identify a failed converter by itself.

questions.claim_review: An inverter-related fault is present while the expected command is not observed. What should be correlated before identifying a root cause?
questions.source_applicability_notes: A missing command is evaluated across command path, communication, enabling, supply/readiness, and fault history rather than assigned to one cause.

questions.claim_review: After service to a power-electronics system, which verification approach best demonstrates that the original concern has been addressed?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Post-repair verification returns to the original concern and relevant system behavior instead of relying on code clearing or replacement alone.

questions.claim_review: For a no-charge concern, which initial evidence set best helps separate an external-supply issue from a vehicle-side readiness issue?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Charging diagnosis is separated across external supply/equipment, connection recognition, vehicle readiness, and battery-side conditions.

questions.claim_review: External charging voltage and the vehicle-side expected input do not agree. What conclusion is justified from that mismatch alone?
questions.source_applicability_notes: A charging voltage mismatch is retained as evidence requiring validation and boundary correlation, not proof that either side is defective.

questions.claim_review: Charging is limited while temperature-related information is present. Which evidence should be correlated to evaluate a thermal-limitation hypothesis?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Thermal charging limitation is evaluated using temperature, thermal status/commands, charging state, context, and applicable criteria.

questions.claim_review: Before considering physical inspection of a thermal-management component, which nonintrusive evidence is most useful to request first?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Nonintrusive thermal/protection status is requested before escalation to physical inspection or higher-risk work.

questions.claim_review: Which approach best evaluates whether a reported temperature value is plausible?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Temperature plausibility is evaluated through related evidence, trends, and context; calibration data alone is not treated as proof.

questions.claim_review: Vehicle output decreases as temperature rises. What evidence pattern would best support, but not by itself prove, a thermal-protection hypothesis?
questions.source_applicability_notes: A repeatable relationship among temperature, protection status, operating state, and derate supports a hypothesis without proving a component fault.

questions.claim_review: Before escalating a communication-loss concern, which foundational evidence should be requested or checked first?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Low-voltage supply, wake-up/readiness, network, module status, and fault history are foundational evidence before escalation.

questions.claim_review: What evidence best indicates whether a control module responded to an expected wake-up request?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Wake-up response is represented as architecture-dependent module status/state evidence interpreted with supply and network context.

questions.claim_review: Several modules report low-voltage or availability concerns at about the same time. Which evidence best supports investigation of a shared cause?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Shared supply, ground, wake-up, network, and timing dependencies are considered before independent module-failure conclusions.

questions.claim_review: In the Request -> Measure -> Compare -> Correlate -> Verify model, what is the purpose of the Request step?
questions.source_applicability_notes: The Request step remains explicitly project-authored; external diagnostic literature supports purposeful evidence gathering and hypothesis-oriented diagnosis without claiming authorship of the framework.

questions.claim_review: A measurement appears inconsistent with other evidence. What action best helps determine whether the measurement itself is reliable?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Repeat/cross-check behavior is used to evaluate measurement consistency; the item does not claim repetition alone proves accuracy.

questions.claim_review: Which documentation best supports a verifiable post-repair record?
questions.source_applicability_notes: Documentation links original concern, evidence, corrective action, and verification results; documentation supports traceability but is not itself the repair verification.
